newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees EMU commitment intact in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees EMU commitment intact in Europe.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Monday that European nations remain committed to monetary union, despite recent signs of uncertainty in Germany and France.
"My impression is that the commitment (to EMU) remains intact," Rubin told reporters.
Rubin declined to specify the impact on the United States if EMU unravels, but added that the process poses no threat to the United States.
"I've never felt that EMU is a threat to us. I've always felt that the principal significance to us ... is the effect it's going to have on Europe," he said.
"If it's good for Europe, it's good for us," Rubin said.
Rubin also declined to comment directly on the recent economic turmoil in Thailand, but added that U.S. officials are watching closely.
"We have been watching and we will continue to be watching and we will continue to discuss it with the appropriate (international) authorities," Rubin said.
